r: Soft potatoes cooked slowly in milk and cream, flavoured with garlic.
Preheat the oven to 160 °C. Peel the potatoes and cut them into thin slices, without washing them.
Heat the milk, cream and crushed garlic with salt, pepper and nutmeg. Add the potatoes and simmer for 10 min, stirring.|Simmer|10
Butter a gratin dish and pour everything in.
Bake for 1 h, until the top is golden and a knife slides in easily.|Oven|60
The cream is replaced with extra milk, and the butter is left out.
The same melt-in-the-mouth texture with just milk: lighter and still delicious.
Preheat the oven to 160 °C. Cut the peeled potatoes into thin slices.
Simmer the milk with the crushed garlic, salt, pepper and nutmeg, add the potatoes and cook for 15 min.|Simmer|15
A layer of grated comté browns on top.
The classic, with a golden, stretchy comté topping.
Preheat the oven to 160 °C. Cut the peeled potatoes into thin slices.
Simmer the milk, cream and garlic with salt, pepper and nutmeg. Add the potatoes and cook for 10 min.|Simmer|10
Pour into a dish and cover with grated comté.
Bake for 1 h, until the cheese is nicely browned.|Oven|60
Grandma's blanquette: tender veal in a creamy lemon sauce, with mushrooms and carrots.
Cut the meat into large cubes and put it in a casserole dish with the sliced carrots, the onion and the bouquet garni. Cover with cold salted water.
Bring to the boil, skim, then cover and simmer for 1 h 30.|Simmer|90
Fry the sliced mushrooms in a little butter for 5 min.|Pan|5
In a saucepan, melt the rest of the butter, add the flour, then 50 cl of the cooking stock, whisking until thickened.
Off the heat, add the cream, the egg yolk and the lemon juice.
Drain the meat and carrots, stir them into the sauce with the mushrooms and serve with rice.
The cream is replaced with fromage blanc and there is no roux.
All the gentleness of blanquette, with a lighter fromage blanc sauce.
Put the cubed meat, sliced carrots, onion and bouquet garni in a casserole dish. Cover with cold salted water.
Bring to the boil, skim and simmer for 1 h 30.|Simmer|90
Add the sliced mushrooms 15 min before the end.
Mix the cornflour with a little cold water, add it to 50 cl of stock and thicken for 2 min, stirring.
Off the heat, add the fromage blanc and lemon juice, then mix with the meat and vegetables.
The veal is replaced with chicken, which cooks twice as fast.
A quicker, cheaper blanquette made with chicken thighs.
Put the chicken, sliced carrots, onion and stock cube in a casserole dish. Cover with water.
Fry the sliced mushrooms in a little butter for 5 min.|Pan|5
Make a roux with the butter and flour, then add 40 cl of stock, whisking.
Add the cream and lemon juice, then the chicken, carrots and mushrooms. Serve with rice.
The ultimate slow-cooked dish: tender beef in red wine, with lardons, mushrooms and baby onions.
Cut the beef into large cubes and brown them in batches in the oil in a casserole dish. Set aside.
Fry the lardons, the sliced onions and the sliced carrots for 5 min.|Cooking|5
Put the meat back, sprinkle with flour and stir for 1 min.
Pour in the wine, add the garlic, bouquet garni, salt and pepper. Top up with water to cover.
Cover and simmer on a low heat for 3 h.|Simmer|180
Add the mushrooms 30 min before the end. Serve with potatoes or pasta.
Cooked in a pressure cooker: 1 h instead of 3 h.
The taste of bourguignon for a weeknight, thanks to the pressure cooker.
Brown the cubed beef in the oil, straight in the pressure cooker, then the lardons and onions.
Sprinkle with flour, stir, then add the wine, sliced carrots, bouquet garni, salt and pepper.
Close the lid and cook for 45 min once the valve starts to hiss.|Pressure cooker|45
Open, add the sliced mushrooms and simmer uncovered for 10 min.|Cooking|10
Mushrooms and root vegetables replace the meat.
A rich, fragrant red wine sauce full of mushrooms and tender vegetables.
Fry the sliced onions in the oil for 5 min in a casserole dish.|Cooking|5
Add the carrots and parsnips in big chunks, then the mushrooms, halved. Brown for 10 min.|Cooking|10
Sprinkle with flour, add the tomato purée, then the wine and 20 cl of water.
Add the thyme, salt and pepper, cover and simmer for 45 min.|Simmer|45
The Sunday family dish: beef cooked for hours in a fragrant broth, with its vegetables.
Put the meat in a large pot, cover with cold water and bring to the boil. Skim.
Add the onion studded with the cloves, the bouquet garni and the coarse salt. Simmer for 2 h.|Simmer|120
Add the carrots, leeks and turnips cut into chunks, and the marrow bones. Cook for 45 min.|Cooking|45
Cook the potatoes separately in a little stock for 25 min.|Cooking|25
Serve the meat and vegetables with coarse salt, mustard and gherkins, and the broth on the side.
A hen or chicken replaces the beef: it is the poule au pot.
A lighter, quicker version with a whole chicken and its vegetables.
Put the chicken in a pot, cover with cold water and bring to the boil. Skim.
Add the onion studded with the cloves, the bouquet garni and the salt. Simmer for 45 min.|Simmer|45
Add the carrots, leeks, turnips and potatoes. Cook for another 40 min.|Cooking|40
Carve the chicken and serve it with the vegetables and a little broth.
In a pressure cooker, the meat is ready in 1 h instead of 3.
The real pot-au-feu, even on a weekday.
Put the meat in the pressure cooker with the onion, bouquet garni and salt. Cover with water and skim as it comes to the boil.
Close the lid and cook for 40 min once the valve starts to hiss.|Pressure cooker|40
Open, add all the vegetables in big chunks, close and cook for 15 min.|Pressure cooker|15
Golden homemade mash on top of seasoned minced meat: pure comfort.
Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water for 20 min.|Cooking|20
Fry the sliced onions and the garlic, then the meat for 8 min. Add salt, pepper and parsley.|Pan|8
Mash the potatoes with the butter and hot milk.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Put the meat in a dish, cover with mash and sprinkle with emmental.
Bake for 20 min, until the top is golden.|Oven|20
The mash is made with half sweet potato, which is sweeter and more colourful.
An orange, slightly sweet mash on minced meat: kids love it.
Boil the peeled sweet potatoes and potatoes in salted water for 20 min.|Cooking|20
Fry the onions, then the meat for 8 min, with salt and pepper.|Pan|8
Mash the vegetables with the butter and milk.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Put the meat in a dish, cover with mash and emmental.
Lentils and carrots replace the minced meat.
Lentils simmered with carrots and tomato, under a golden mash.
Boil the lentils in unsalted water for 25 min.|Cooking|25
Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water for 20 min, then mash them with the butter and milk.|Cooking|20
Fry the diced onion and carrots for 10 min, then add the drained lentils and the tomato purée.|Pan|10
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Put the lentils in a dish, cover with mash and emmental.
The real quiche lorraine: crisp pastry, lardons and a creamy egg filling.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Roll the pastry into a tin and prick the base.
Fry the lardons in a pan for 5 min with no added fat, and spread them over the pastry.|Pan|5
Beat the eggs with the cream, milk, a little salt, pepper and the nutmeg.
Pour over the lardons and bake for 35 min, until golden.|Oven|35
The cream is replaced with milk and the lardons with ham.
All the flavour of quiche, with a lighter filling.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Roll the pastry into a tin and prick the base.
Spread the diced ham over the pastry.
Beat the eggs with the milk, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Pour in and bake for 35 min.|Oven|35
The lardons are replaced with softened leeks and goat's cheese.
A mild, fragrant quiche with soft leeks and goat's cheese.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Roll the pastry into a tin.
Slice the leeks and soften them in the butter for 10 min.|Pan|10
Beat the eggs with the cream, milk, salt and pepper.
Spread the leeks over the pastry, pour in the filling and add the goat's cheese in slices.
The golden, melting croque, with ham, emmental and a touch of béchamel.
Make a small béchamel: melt 15 g of butter, add the flour, then the milk, whisking for 3 min.|Béchamel|3
Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Lightly butter the outside of the bread slices.
Top 4 slices with béchamel, ham and emmental, then cover with the other slices.
Add a little béchamel and emmental on top.
Bake for 10 min, until nicely golden.|Oven|10
A fried egg is placed on top of the croque.
The croque-monsieur, topped with a runny fried egg.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Butter the outside of the bread slices.
Top 4 slices with ham and emmental, cover with the other slices and sprinkle with emmental.
Meanwhile, fry the eggs for 3 min.|Pan|3
Put an egg on each croque and serve.
The ham is replaced with tomato and mushrooms.
A tasty croque with mushrooms, tomato and emmental.
Fry the sliced mushrooms in a little butter for 5 min.|Pan|5
Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Butter the outside of the bread slices.
Top 4 slices with mushrooms, tomato slices and emmental, then cover.
Sprinkle with emmental and bake for 10 min.|Oven|10
The great slow-cooked classic: tender chicken in a red wine sauce, with lardons and mushrooms.
coq au vin chicken red wine
Brown the chicken pieces in the oil in a casserole dish. Set aside.
Fry the lardons, onions and carrots for 5 min.|Cooking|5
Put the chicken back, sprinkle with flour and stir.
Pour in the wine, add the garlic, bouquet garni, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 1 h 15.|Simmer|75
Add the mushrooms and cook for another 20 min.|Cooking|20
The red wine is replaced with white wine and a little cream.
A milder version made with white wine, in a creamy sauce.
Brown the chicken in the oil in a casserole dish, then the lardons and onions.
Pour in the white wine, add the thyme, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 50 min.|Simmer|50
Add the sliced mushrooms and cook for 15 min.|Cooking|15
Add the cream and let it reduce for 5 min.|Cooking|5
With boneless thighs, it is ready in under an hour.
The taste of the classic, on a weeknight.
Brown the chicken in the oil for 8 min, then the lardons and the sliced onion.|Cooking|8
Sprinkle with flour, pour in the wine, add salt and pepper.
Add the mushrooms, cover and simmer for 30 min.|Simmer|30
Chicken simmered with peppers, tomatoes and Espelette pepper: the sunshine of the Basque Country.
Brown the chicken pieces in the oil in a casserole dish. Set aside.
Fry the onions, garlic and sliced peppers for 10 min.|Cooking|10
Add the chopped tomatoes, the wine, the Espelette pepper, salt and pepper.
Put the chicken back, cover and simmer for 45 min.|Simmer|45
Chicken breasts and tinned tomatoes: ready in 30 minutes.
The flavours of basquaise, for a busy evening.
Cut the chicken into pieces and brown it in the oil for 5 min.|Pan|5
Add the onion, garlic and sliced peppers, and cook for 8 min.|Cooking|8
Pour in the tomatoes, add the Espelette pepper, salt and pepper, and simmer for 15 min.|Simmer|15
The chicken is replaced with chickpeas.
Slow-cooked piperade and tender chickpeas, for a sunny veggie dish.
Fry the onion, garlic and sliced peppers in the oil for 10 min.|Cooking|10
Add the chopped tomatoes, the Espelette pepper, salt and pepper, and simmer for 15 min.|Simmer|15
Add the drained chickpeas and cook for another 5 min.|Cooking|5
A golden, crispy chicken with homemade gravy and roast potatoes.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C. Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 min beforehand.
Rub the chicken with the soft butter, salt, pepper and thyme. Put the garlic inside.
Place it in a dish, surrounded by the potatoes cut into chunks and tossed in oil.
Pour a glass of water into the dish and bake for 1 h 15, basting every 20 min.|Oven|75
Rest for 10 min under a sheet of foil before carving.|Rest|10
The chicken is flavoured with lemon, garlic and rosemary.
A fresh roast chicken with lemon and rosemary.
Put a lemon cut into quarters, the garlic and the rosemary inside the chicken. Rub it with oil, salt and pepper.
Surround it with the potatoes and the other lemon in wedges.
Legs instead of a whole chicken: half the cooking time.
The taste of Sunday chicken, in 45 minutes.
Mix the oil, paprika, thyme, salt and pepper, and brush over the legs.
Put them in a dish with the potatoes in wedges and the garlic.
Bake for 40 min, until the skin is really crispy.|Oven|40
